title: Intake re-check before triage: an issue already fixed on base closes with evidence

story.i_want_to: check an incoming issue against what base already contains before I spend a triage dispatch on it
story.so_that: an issue a merged change already fixed is closed with the proof, and no holder spends a session on it

rationale: PRD R6: 'Before triage, intake checks whether the issue is already fixed, a duplicate, or no longer reproduces, and closes it with the evidence.' Today TriageTrigger.promote/1 (triage_trigger.ex:108) creates the stub at detected and TriageDispatcher (triage_dispatcher.ex:141) dispatches triage@1 for every candidate, so an issue a merged PR already closed still costs a three-lens triage session; IssueClosure carries a verdict and a label but no evidence (issue_closure.ex:63-79). This story adds the re-check step to the triage dispatch pass, the first of three findings (already fixed), and the evidence field every auto-close carries from now on.

acceptance_criteria.description: Loopctl.Delivery.IntakeRecheck.run/2 (tenant_id, story) runs inside TriageDispatchWorker's pass before TriageDispatcher.run/1, over stories at detected that have an intake record, whose source is not paused, and that have no 'rechecked' event since their newest entry into detected; it writes one 'rechecked' event with data %{findings: [...], checked_at, base_sha}.

triage@1's candidate predicates gain :rechecked, so TriageDispatcher.candidates/1 returns a detected story only after a 'rechecked' event newer than its newest entry into detected; a story re-entering detected (retriage, human re-triage) is re-checked again.

The finding already_fixed holds when the record's chg finding (Findings.for_record/1) has state fixed with a fix_merge_sha that PullRequestSource.contains?/3 reports in the source's base branch, or when the new callback PullRequestSource.closing_references/3 returns a merged pull request into the base branch whose body or title closes the issue number with a GitHub closing keyword and whose merge commit base contains.

An already_fixed story moves detected -> done over the new control-only edge :recheck_fixed in the same transaction as the 'rechecked' event; StageMachine.resolution_verdict/1 maps it to the new verdict :already_fixed, which Resolution maps to the existing loopctl:resolution-not-actionable label with its own resolution text naming the fix.

issue_closures gains evidence (text, at most 2000 codepoints, built from loopctl-held facts only: PR number and URL, merge sha, finding id, ledger row ids), set for every verdict a re-check reaches, and IssueCloser posts it as an 'Evidence' section of the closing comment after the resolution text.
A forge call that fails or times out records the finding forge_unavailable in the 'rechecked' event and lets the story proceed to triage, so a forge outage never holds an issue at detected.

Running the pass twice over the same story writes one 'rechecked' event and at most one transition: the event write is guarded by the stage row lock and the 'no rechecked event since entry' condition re-read under it.
An issue no merged change closes is not closed: the 'rechecked' event lists finding none and the story reaches TriageDispatcher.candidates/1 in the same pass.

technical_notes: Where it runs: TriageDispatchWorker (oban_config.ex:691, every minute) calls IntakeRecheck before TriageDispatcher.run/1 (lib/loopctl/delivery/triage_dispatcher.ex:141). Why not TriageTrigger.promote/1 (triage_trigger.ex:108): promote creates the stub inside a transaction on intake facts only and runs per record; a forge call there would hold the record lock across the network. The re-check is its own pass on the stub, so the stub is the single item every finding is recorded against.

Candidates: :rechecked joins Loopctl.Agents.Candidates' predicate set (lib/loopctl/agents/candidates.ex:101-134) and triage@1's list (lib/loopctl/agents/specs/triage_v1.ex); :intake_not_paused is provided by US-52.33.

Facts: Findings.for_record/1 (lib/loopctl/changes/findings.ex:584) and Finding fields state, fix_merge_sha (lib/loopctl/changes/finding.ex:31-54); PullRequestSource.contains?/3 (lib/loopctl/delivery/pull_request_source.ex:274); the new callback closing_references/3 joins the behaviour (:173-365) and GithubPullRequestSource uses the issues search API under its existing timeouts and token.

Closing keywords: close, closes, closed, fix, fixes, fixed, resolve, resolves, resolved, followed by #N or owner/repo#N for the source's repo, case-insensitive; a mention without a keyword is not evidence.

Edge and verdict: add {:detected, :done, :recheck_fixed} to @transitions (stage_machine.ex:286) as control-only (refused by Stages.advance/4 from other callers, stages.ex:2114) and to @resolution_verdicts (:708) as :already_fixed; Resolution (lib/loopctl/delivery/resolution.ex:65-128) gains :already_fixed in @verdicts and for_verdict/1, keeping the two labels, because the reporting system binds to labels/0.

Evidence: issue_closures migration adds evidence; Stages.record_issue_closure/3 (stages.ex:981) takes it from the transition's event data; IssueCloser (lib/loopctl/delivery/issue_closer.ex) appends it. Evidence is built only from loopctl's records and forge fields it parsed (numbers, shas, URLs), never from issue or PR text, so it carries no reporter content.
The 'rechecked' event is a non-stage event of the work-item event log provided by release 3 (README names table: work-item event log); its data never carries forge text.
Docs: docs/agent-delivery-loop.md intake section and CHANGELOG.md (new edge, verdict, closing comment section).
non_goals: Re-opening an issue a re-check closed in error: the reporter reopens it, and the existing reopen path makes a new generation.

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.36.6: a forge that cannot be reached is a forge_unavailable finding and triage proceeds; the re-check never blocks an issue on the forge.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.36.1: the re-check's result is a 'rechecked' event in the append-only log; a crash before it is written leaves the story at detected with no event, and the next pass re-checks it.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.36.7: the event and any transition are written once under the stage row lock, so a retried or concurrent pass is a no-op.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.36.6: each forge call runs under PullRequestSource's timeout and the pass checks at most the TriageDispatcher batch size per run, so a slow forge delays one batch and falls back to forge_unavailable.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.36.1: the step runs inside the existing minute TriageDispatchWorker cron on any node; a story missed by a dead node is picked up by the next run.

definition_of_done: On production, a sandbox issue opened after a merged sandbox PR that says 'Fixes #N' is closed within five minutes with the not-actionable label and a comment carrying an Evidence section naming that PR.
SELECT count(*) FROM runner_dispatches WHERE kind = 'triage' AND story_id = <that item> returns 0.
defaults: already_fixed closes with the existing loopctl:resolution-not-actionable label and its own text, so HomeCareBilling's label binding keeps working.
A forge outage lets triage proceed rather than holding the issue.
Evidence at most 2000 codepoints, loopctl facts only.
